rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a human voice as a sound and, in context, the usable power of speaking.

example.jyutping: nei5 ge3 sing1 jam1 gei2 hou2 teng1 wo3

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose spoken choice when someone puts words to a thought, feeling, or opinion.

example.english: I want to voice my feelings.
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 gong2 ceot1 zi6 gei2 ge3 gam2 sau6

rows.note: Choose this when the emphasis is on expressing a sentiment, view, or position rather than simply saying it aloud.

example.english: I want to voice my support for you in a letter.
example.traditional: 我想用一封信表達對你嘅支持。
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 jung6 jat1 fung1 seon3 biu2 daat6 deoi3 nei5 ge3 zi1 ci4

rows.note: Use this when voicing something means making an official public announcement.

example.english: The company will voice its decision to give everyone a raise today.
example.jyutping: gung1 si1 gam1 jat6 syun1 bou3 gaa1 jan4 gung1

rows.note: Choose this for publicly issuing or publishing an opinion, statement, or other formal utterance.

example.english: The government will voice its position on the incident.
example.jyutping: zing3 fu2 zau6 si6 gin6 faat3 biu2 lap6 coeng4

rows.note: Use this when “voice” means an actual vote or ballot in a decision.

example.english: This time, I’m casting my voice for him.
example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 ngo5 zoeng1 piu3 tau4 bei2 keoi5

rows.note: Use this when “voice” means the right or ability to express an opinion and have it considered, rather than a ballot.

example.english: Those residents finally have a voice.
example.traditional: 嗰班街坊終於有發言權喇。
example.jyutping: go2 baan1 gaai1 fong1 zung1 jyu1 jau5 faat3 jin4 kyun4 laa3

rows.note: Use this for the distinctive tone or style of someone’s writing.

example.english: I really like the voice of your writing.
example.traditional: 我幾鍾意你篇文嘅文風。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gei2 zung1 ji3 nei5 pin1 man4 ge3 man4 fung1
